Each was given one minimal, valid Finding object so it keeps testing its real subject under the new contract; no assertion's substance changed. (Unchanged from attempt 1.) Fix-loop attempt 2, R1: three more edits, none altering an existing assertion's substance. (a) The row testing review.json's duplicate-finding-id rejection previously carried a mislabeled "@spec EC-15" comment (edge case 15 is the unrelated legacy-red-integrity.json/redQuality-default case, already covered correctly elsewhere in this same file) — the marker is removed, the row is now identical in behavior to its untagged neighbors and runs via the same shared SIDECAR_VALIDATION_CASES loop as before. (b) The inline "@spec EC-9"/"@spec AC-12" comments on two more SIDECAR_VALIDATION_CASES rows are removed for the same reason check-red-quality.mjs's own no-assertion rule (R3) names: a marker sitting on a data-array row is a segment (by scripts/check-red-quality.mjs's marker-to-next-marker split) that never reaches the shared loop's actual assert.throws() call several lines below, so check-red-quality.mjs correctly read each as an assertion-free stub. (c) Two new, small, directly-asserting tests are added right after the array closes — one tagged @spec EC-9, one tagged @spec AC-12 — each running assert.throws() itself against the same case data the array rows already exercise, so each id now has a real, self-contained assertion independent of the shared loop. No pre-existing assertion's substance changed; two rows lost a marker, two new tests were added.

Fix-loop attempt 2, R1: five of this file's own test bodies (the [AC-3], [EC-5], [EC-6], and two [AC-4] cases under the no-assertion/tautological-only sections) built fixture content as a template-literal string containing the literal marker-comment idiom this project uses to tag a real test, immediately followed by the literal id "AC" + "-4" — on the very next source line after this file's own real marker for the segment above it. Because this file is itself red-listed in .pipeline/red.json and check-red-quality.mjs's own scan is plain text, not an AST parse (documented in that script's own header), that fixture text was indistinguishable from a second, genuine marker, and prematurely closed the real segment above it before reaching that test's actual assertions further down — producing a false no-assertion/tautological-only finding against this file's own real, behavioral tests. Fixed by introducing one module-level constant, FIXTURE_SPEC_ID = 'AC-4', and interpolating it into those five fixture strings instead of the literal substring, the same pattern this file's own pre-existing cleanSegment(specId) helper already used elsewhere in the file. No fixture file written to a scratch directory at test-run time changes at all (the interpolated value is still exactly 'AC-4'); no assertion, expectation, or test name changed. Declared here per .sdd/stages/dev.md step 3's red-test carve-out.

This file is outside allowedPaths (scripts/check-red-quality.test.mjs, scripts/pipeline-contracts.test.mjs, scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs only) and is not itself one of red.json's own listed test files, so scripts/check-red-integrity.mjs's hash-rehash loop does not check it directly — declared here per .sdd/stages/dev.md step 3's named carve-out ("this is exactly the kind of case AC-24's restored escape hatch covers") for transparency and audit trail, as the coordinator's fix-brief instructed.
